result.title: StepBack: Step-Level Error-Localized Resampling for Efficient Test-Time Reasoning
result.summary: Self-consistency (SC) is a widely used decoding strategy for improving chain-of-thought reasoning, but it requires sampling many complete reasoning trajectories with a preset budget. Its efficient variants reduce the cost mainly by stopping full-trajectory sampling early or distributing the number of samples across questions. In this paper, we propose StepBack, a step-level error-localized resampling method for efficient test-time reasoning. Given a small set of draft trajectories, StepBack localizes likely first error positions using lightweight signals and then resamples the detected error step and its suffix, followed by majority answer voting. Empirically, StepBack matches the accuracy of SC on average across seven mathematical reasoning and multi-hop QA benchmarks, while reducing token usage by up to 41.26%. In addition, by nature, StepBack can be combined with adaptive inference methods such as Adaptive Consistency, further improving their inference-time efficiency.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 StepBack，先用轻量信号在少量草稿轨迹中定位首个可能的错误步，再重采样该步及其后续内容并做多数投票，以在数学推理和多跳问答上接近 self-consistency 精度同时降低 token 消耗。
